newsitem.title: CANADA: Some Canada exporters close to annual lumber quota.
newsitem.headline: Some Canada exporters close to annual lumber quota.

text.p: Some Canadian softwood lumber exporters are very close to or may already have reached their annual limits for shipments to the United States, a source familiar with the situation said on Monday.
"There are some who are very close, there might even be some who are at their quota," the source told Reuters.

Canada suspended issuing lumber export permits for two days on October 30 in a bid to streamline its export system, which had shifted from a first-come-first-served basis to individual company export quotas.
The company quotas, which are confidential, were sent to lumber exporters on October 31 by Canada's International Trade Department. It is up to the companies to reveal their limits if they want to.
But some of them may have already reached their annual allocations and would face export fees if they chose to continue shipments south of the border, the source said.

Under an agreement between Canada and the United States that took effect on April 1, Canadian lumber shipments which exceed 14.7 billion board feet annually, or 4.226 billion board feet quarterly, are subject to export fees.
Canada on Friday said it would resume issuing export permits on November 1 and publishing daily export statistics on November 4. As of 1620 EST/2120 GMT on Monday no statistics had been published.
